doc.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023

title: A studio day and the Tonight Show job after John Audino's death
summary: Rowe asks about a typical day; Findley tells of touring Germany with Herbolzheimer and Doc Severinsen calling his wife after Audino died.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: That’s a fascinating backstory to all that. I want to take you back to your busy studio life. I came across one of those on-line Chuck Findley discographies, you know, the never- ending scroll. And I started to count, literally, and I said this is not going to work. But what I did see is that in 1979, according to this list, you played on 26 LPs. Like that’s more than two a month and everybody from Dolly Parton to Tom Scott. So I don’t have a question, it’s simply an observation. But I wonder if you can describe, let’s jump ten years later, 1989, a day in the life of Chuck Findley when you were on the Tonight Show band, what was a typical weekday like for you?

Well that was wonderful actually. Well it was not really nice, I mean John Audino had passed away and I was in Germany. I was doing a little tour with Peter Herbolzheimer in Germany. And I was considering actually moving there because our son was young and I wanted him to get the culture and learn other languages other than just English. I wanted him to learn German and go to schools there. They know three or four languages everybody over there. They speak and you feel like a fool when I went over there the first time just speaking English and you know, learning a few words here and there. But we don’t get that training here you know. Then once again if I went to Oregon there would be another language, or if I went to Nevada it would be a different language. So Europe is different in that aspect. But in ’89 John Audino passed away and I was in Germany and I was in Hamburg. And actually Doc Severinsen called my wife to tell her first and to find out where I was and she said that I was in Hamburg, Germany. And he told her about Johnny passing, and that he would love me to do the gig. And Johnny and I were so close and just wonderful, what a marvelous man and player he was. And in that trumpet section was Conte Candoli and Snooky and Johnny and Maury Harris. Well Johnny had passed. So Doc and I go way back to 1965 when I first met Doc. But that was another story, I could tell you that real quick if you want.
